problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\pi $ for the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$
worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t),$ we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,{e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨{e}^{\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ),\,{e}^{\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{\pi },\,-{e}^{\pi }⟩ \\  & ={e}^{\pi }⟨-1,\,-1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & ={e}^{\pi }\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t))⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\pi ) & =⟨-2{e}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,2{e}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & ={e}^{\pi }⟨0,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and ${r}^{″}(\pi )$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi ) & ={e}^{\pi }⟨-1,\,-1,\,0⟩\times {e}^{\pi }⟨0,\,-2,\,0⟩ \\  & ={({e}^{\pi })}^{2}\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & -1 & 0 \\ \,0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & ={e}^{2\pi }\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ \,0 & -2\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =2{e}^{2\pi }\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖ & =2{e}^{2\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=\pi $ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\pi ) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\pi ){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖}=\frac{{(\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{\pi })}^{3}}{\,2{e}^{2\pi }\,}=\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
